issues.legal_issue: An objection to execution that was previously dismissed for default is not barred by res judicata when the objection was not heard and finally decided.
material_facts: In the course of execution of a mortgage decree, judgment debtors raised an objection that the decree could not be executed under the applicable land-reform law.
Two earlier applications raising the same objection were dismissed for the judgment debtors’ default, without a decision on the objection’s merits.
A later application raised the same objection, which the execution court considered and decided.
issues.conclusion: The objection was not barred by res judicata because the earlier applications had been dismissed for default and the objection had not been heard and finally decided.
issues.legal_principle: Res judicata, whether under section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure or as a matter of public policy, requires that the issue or plea have been heard and finally decided. The Court relied on Maharaja Radha Parshad Singh v. Lal Sahab Rai, Pulvarthi Venkata Subba Rao v. Velluri Jagannadha Rao, Lakshmibai Anant Kondkar v. Ravji Bhikaji Kondkar, Bahir Das Pal v. Girish Chandra Pal, Bhagwati Prasad Sah v. Radha Kishun Sah, Jethmal v. Mst. Sakina, and Bishwanath Kundu v. Subala Dassi; it disapproved Ramnarain v. Basudeo.

predicates.execution_proceeding: The dispute arose in proceedings to execute a decree.
predicates.earlier_objections_dismissed_for_default: The objecting judgment debtor’s earlier applications raising the objection were dismissed for default.
predicates.objection_not_decided_on_merits: The earlier dismissals did not follow a hearing and final decision on the objection’s merits.
predicates.repeated_objection_not_barred_by_res_jud: The same objection may be raised again without being barred by res judicata.

issues.definition: When an execution objection was previously dismissed for default without a decision on its merits, raising it again in execution is not barred by res judicata.

issues.legal_issue: Execution of a mortgage decree for money secured by an estate cannot proceed after the entire mortgaged estate vests in the State, even where certain lands are settled back with the former proprietor as raiyat.
material_facts: The mortgage decree covered an estate, including Bakasht lands and other lands.
The entire estate covered by the notification vested in the State under the land-reform law.
Certain lands, including the Bakasht lands, were deemed settled by the State with the former proprietor, who held them as a raiyat.
The decree-holders sought to execute the mortgage decree against the Bakasht lands after vesting and had applied to have their compensation determined under the Act.
issues.conclusion: The mortgage decree could not be executed against the Bakasht lands. The decree-holders’ remedy was to pursue their claim through the Act’s compensation procedure.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 3, 4 and 6 of the Bihar Land Reforms Act, 1950, the notified estate first vests in the State free of encumbrances; the later deemed settlement of raiyat rights in specified lands does not mean those lands never vested. Section 4(d) bars suits and proceedings for recovery of money secured by a mortgage of an estate and includes execution proceedings. The creditor’s remedy is the claim procedure under Chapter IV, including section 14; section 24(5) addresses payment of compensation to a mortgage creditor. The Court relied on Rana Sheo Ambar Singh v. Allahabad Bank Ltd., Krishna Prasad v. Gauri Kumari Devi, and Raj Kishore v. Ram Pratap, and rejected the contrary majority view in Sidheshwar Prasad Singh v. Ram Saroop Singh.

rule.if: mortgage_execution_proceeding and debt_secured_by_estate_mortgage and entire_mortgaged_estate_vested and some_lands_settled_back_to_former_owner

predicates.mortgage_execution_proceeding: A decree-holder sought to recover a mortgage debt through execution proceedings.
predicates.debt_secured_by_estate_mortgage: Payment of the debt was secured by a mortgage of an estate.
predicates.entire_mortgaged_estate_vested: The whole estate covered by the mortgage vested in the State.
predicates.some_lands_settled_back_to_former_owner: The State settled certain lands with the former proprietor to be held under a new raiyat right.
predicates.execution_cannot_proceed: The mortgage decree cannot be enforced through execution against the lands in the vested estate.

issues.definition: When execution seeks recovery of a debt secured by an estate mortgage, the entire mortgaged estate has vested, and some lands have been settled back with the former proprietor, execution cannot proceed.
